info.title: Convert API
info.description:
Converts office documents and PDFs into a standard PDF and per-page images.

One call does the whole job. Upload a file, say what you want back, and
receive either the PDF itself or a tar.zst bundle holding the PDF, the page
images and a `manifest.json` that describes them.

## Authentication

Every `/v1` route needs the service API key as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
```

The probes (`/healthz`, `/readyz`) take no key.

## Calling it

```bash
# Office document to PDF (the default output)
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONVERT_API_KEY" \
  -F file=@deck.pptx \
  -o deck.pdf \
  "$CONVERT_HOST/v1/convert"

# PDF plus page images at 150 DPI, as one tar.zst bundle
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONVERT_API_KEY" \
  -F file=@deck.pptx \
  -F 'options={"output":"bundle","images":{"format":"jpeg","dpi":150}};type=application/json' \
  -o deck.tar.zst \
  "$CONVERT_HOST/v1/convert"

# First page of an existing PDF as a small thumbnail
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONVERT_API_KEY" \
  -F file=@report.pdf \
  -F 'options={"output":"images","pages":"1","images":{"format":"jpeg","dpi":72,"max_edge":320}};type=application/json' \
  -o thumb.tar.zst \
  "$CONVERT_HOST/v1/convert"
```

## What comes back

The `output` option decides the response. Each value maps to exactly one
content type:

| `output` | Response | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pdf` (default) | `application/pdf` | The PDF. Metadata travels in `Convert-*` headers. |
| `images` | `application/zstd` | `manifest.json` and `pages/NNNN.<ext>`, as tar.zst |
| `bundle` | `application/zstd` | `manifest.json`, `document.pdf` and `pages/NNNN.<ext>`, as tar.zst |

The response is only sent once the whole job has succeeded, so a `200`
always carries a complete result and every failure has a proper status
code and JSON error body.

## Errors and retries

Every error body is `{"error": "<message>", "code": "<CODE>"}`.

| Status | Codes | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | No. The request is malformed. |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | No. |
| 413 | `FILE_TOO_LARGE` | No. |
| 415 | `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT` | No. |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`, `INVALID_PASSWORD`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `CONVERSION_FAILED` | No. The same input will fail the same way. |
| 429 | `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` | Yes, after `Retry-After` seconds. |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Yes, with backoff. |
| 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | Yes, after `Retry-After` seconds. |
| 504 | `CONVERSION_TIMEOUT` | Once at most. A second timeout means the document is too heavy for the budget. |

The service already retries a crashed engine once on a fresh worker, so
`CONVERSION_FAILED` is final.

## Determinism and caching

The service keeps no state and stores nothing after the response is sent.
The same file, options and engine build produce the same output, so callers
can cache results under `sha256(file) + options + Convert-Engine-Fingerprint`.
The fingerprint changes whenever output could change: a new service
version, LibreOffice version, PDFium version or font set.

get.description: Returns 200 while the supervisor process is running. Checks nothing else.
Metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format.

Returns 200 when every worker pool has at least one warm worker and
the service is not shutting down. Returns 503 while starting, while
draining, or when a pool has no healthy worker.

503.description: Not ready. Do not route traffic here.

get.summary: List supported formats, limits and engine versions
get.description:
Describes what this deployment can do: which input formats it accepts,
which outputs it produces, the limits it enforces, the engine versions
it runs and the fonts it has installed.

The answer is fixed for the lifetime of a deployment, so clients can
read it once at start-up.

parameters.name: X-Request-ID
parameters.description:
Correlation ID. If present it is echoed in the response, the logs and
the manifest. If absent the service generates one.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

post.summary: Convert one document to PDF, page images, or both
post.description:
Uploads one file and returns it as a PDF, as page images, or as a
bundle of both.

**Routing.** The file type is detected from the bytes, never from the
file name or the part's content type. Office and OpenDocument files go
through LibreOffice. PDFs skip conversion and go straight to rendering.
Image files (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF, BMP, WebP) are not accepted as
input and answer 415 `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT`.

**Options.** Send them as a JSON object in the `options` part. Leave
the part out to get a PDF with default settings. Unknown properties
are rejected with `VALIDATION_ERROR` so that typos never pass silently.

**Timing.** The call is synchronous. `timeout_seconds` is the whole
budget from the end of the upload to the response headers: queueing,
conversion, rendering and packaging. When it runs out the engine
process is killed and the call returns `CONVERSION_TIMEOUT`. Streaming
the body comes after it and is not part of that budget. The server cuts
a body that the client stops reading, or reads below the deployment's
minimum rate; the same holds for an upload that stalls or trickles.

**Safety.** Macros never run, external links are never fetched and the
engine has no network access. A document that relies on any of those
still converts, without that content.

parameters.name: X-Request-ID
parameters.description:
Correlation ID. If present it is echoed in the response, the logs and
the manifest. If absent the service generates one.

200.description:
The conversion succeeded. The content type follows the `output`
option: `application/pdf` for `pdf`, `application/zstd` for
`images` and `bundle`.

The `application/zstd` body is a ustar archive in one zstd frame
(`<stem>.tar.zst`), sent chunked without `Content-Length`. Its entries,
in this order:

```
manifest.json        described by the Manifest schema
document.pdf         only for output=bundle
pages/0001.jpg       one file per rendered page, 1-based, zero-padded
pages/0002.jpg
```

Every entry is a regular file, mode 0644, mtime 0, uid and gid 0.

Read the body to the end before you use it: a stream that ends early is not a valid archive.

Content-Disposition.description: `attachment` with a file name derived from the upload, for example `deck.pdf` or `deck.tar.zst`.

Convert-Engine-Fingerprint.description:
Identifies everything that decides the output bytes: service version,
LibreOffice version, PDFium version, installed font set, and the
deployment settings that change the output (render caps, default paper
size, the blank-page probe). Use it in cache keys.

Convert-Page-Count.description: Number of pages in the resulting PDF.

Convert-Source-Format.description: The detected input format, as listed by `/v1/capabilities`.

Convert-Warning-Count.description:
Number of warnings raised for this conversion. The warnings
themselves are in `manifest.json`; ask for `bundle` to read them.

Server-Timing.description:
Where the time of this request went, in the W3C Server-Timing form
`name;dur=<milliseconds>`, comma-separated, with 3 decimals. It is
sent on every response produced after the file type was detected,
including the error responses that follow detection. It is meant for
diagnosis and benchmarks.

| Name | Stage |
| --- | --- |
| `recv` | Receiving the upload. Outside `total`. |
| `detect` | Detecting the file type. |
| `preflight` | The office worker's scan of an office source, inside `convert` before the engine opens the file. Counted as overhead. |
| `queue` | Waiting for a free worker. |
| `lease` | Taking the worker from its pool. |
| `spawn` | Starting a worker on this request's path. 0 when a warm worker was used. |
| `bind` | Loading the engine library in that worker. 0 when a warm worker was used. |
| `convert`, `convert_engine` | Producing the PDF: wall time, then time inside the engine. |
| `inspect`, `inspect_engine` | Reading the PDF's facts: wall time, then engine time. |
| `probe`, `probe_engine` | The blank-page probe: wall time, then engine time. |
| `render`, `render_engine` | Rendering page images: wall time, then engine time (the longest chunk). |
| `verify` | The quality checks that raise warnings. |
| `package` | Building the manifest and the bundle plan before the headers are sent. |
| `total` | From the end of the upload to the start of the response. |

Stages that did not run are left out, except `spawn` and `bind`.
Server-Timing.example: recv;dur=4.210, detect;dur=0.031, queue;dur=0.004, lease;dur=0.012, spawn;dur=0.000, bind;dur=0.000, convert;dur=812.442, convert_engine;dur=809.118, verify;dur=1.305, package;dur=0.088, total;dur=815.901

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

fonts.description: Installed font families, sorted by name.

inputs.description: Every input format this deployment accepts.

ConvertOptions.description:
What to produce and how. Every property is optional. An empty object,
or no `options` part at all, returns a PDF with default settings.

pages.description:
Which pages to render as images, 1-based. A comma-separated list of
single pages (`3`), closed ranges (`1-5`) and open ranges (`10-`).
Pages past the end of the document are ignored. If nothing is
left the call fails with `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

Applies to `images` and `bundle`. The PDF always holds every page.
Default: all pages.

password.description:
Password for an encrypted input. It is used once to open the file,
never logged and never stored. The resulting PDF is not encrypted.

timeout_seconds.description:
Total time budget for this call, in seconds. Covers waiting for a
worker, conversion, rendering and packaging. The server caps it at
`limits.max_timeout_seconds`.

file.description:
The document to convert. The part's file name is used only to name
the response and is echoed in the manifest. The type is detected
from the bytes.

EngineInfo.description: The software that produced the result.

libreoffice.description: LibreOffice version. Absent from a manifest when LibreOffice was not used.

error.description: A human-readable message. Safe to log; never contains document content.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Branch on this, not on the message.

FormatFamily.description: The broad kind of input, which decides how it is routed.

ImageFormat.description:
Image encoding.

- `jpeg`: smallest and fastest. Best for photos, slides and model input.
- `png`: lossless. Larger and slower to encode.

ImageOptions.description: How pages are rendered to images. Used by `images` and `bundle`.

dpi.description:
Render resolution in dots per inch. A US Letter page is
1275 x 1650 px at 150 DPI. The server caps it at `limits.max_dpi`.

max_edge.description:
Longest allowed edge of an image, in pixels. A page that would be
larger is rendered at a lower resolution so that it fits, keeping
its aspect ratio. Unset means no clamp beyond `limits.max_edge_px`.

ImageSettings.description: The image settings that were actually applied, after defaults and server caps.

engine.description: Which engine turns this format into a PDF. `pdfium` means the file already is one.

format.description: Short identifier, used in `Convert-Source-Format` and the manifest.

max_render_pages.description: Most pages one call may render to images.

Manifest.description:
The `manifest.json` at the root of every tar.zst response. It describes
the source, the PDF, each rendered page and anything the service
noticed during conversion.

page_count.description: Number of pages in the PDF, whether or not all were rendered.

pages.description: One entry per rendered page, in page order.

request_id.description: The correlation ID of the request that produced this bundle.

warnings.description: Things the service noticed that may affect quality. Empty when all checks passed.

warnings.message: Aptos is not installed and was replaced by Carlito

OutputKind.description:
What the response contains.

- `pdf`: the PDF, as `application/pdf`.
- `images`: page images and a manifest, as `application/zstd` (tar.zst).
- `bundle`: the PDF, page images and a manifest, as `application/zstd` (tar.zst).

blank.description: True when the rendered page is a single flat colour.

height_pt.description: Page height in PDF points (1/72 inch).

path.description: Path of the image inside the archive.

width_pt.description: Page width in PDF points (1/72 inch).

PdfInfo.description: The PDF inside a `bundle`. Absent for `images`.

origin.description:
How the PDF came to be.

- `converted`: produced by LibreOffice from an office file.
- `passthrough`: the upload was already a PDF and is returned unchanged, or decrypted when it was encrypted.

path.description: Path of the PDF inside the archive.

idle.description: Warm workers waiting for a job.

status.description:
- `ready`: taking conversions.
- `starting`: workers are still warming up.
- `draining`: shutting down; in-flight jobs are finishing.
- `degraded`: a pool has no healthy worker.

commit.description: Git commit the binary was built from.

one_page_per_sheet.description:
Put each sheet on a single page sized to its content, instead of
splitting it across pages by its print layout.

SlideNotes.description:
What to do with speaker notes.

- `none`: slides only.
- `append`: all slides, followed by one notes page per slide.
- `only`: notes pages only.

include_hidden.description: Also export slides that are marked hidden.

filename.description: The file name sent with the upload, if any.

format.description: The detected format, as listed by `/v1/capabilities`.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the uploaded bytes, in lowercase hex.

Timings.description: Where the time went, in milliseconds.

convert.description: Producing the PDF. Zero for PDF uploads.

total.description: From the end of the upload to the start of the response.

Warning.description: A quality signal. Warnings never fail the request.

detail.description: Structured data for the warning. Its keys depend on `code`.

page.description: The page the warning is about, when it concerns one page.

WarningCode.description:
- `FONT_SUBSTITUTED`: a font the document asks for is not installed.
  `detail.substitute` is the font that the image's fontconfig picked
  for it when the image was built, not one read from the PDF.
  Text may reflow. `detail` has `requested` and `substitute`.
- `PAGE_COUNT_MISMATCH`: the PDF has a different number of pages than
  the source declares. `detail` has `expected` and `actual`.
- `BLANK_PAGE`: a page that contains content rendered as a flat colour.
- `MACROS_IGNORED`: the document contains macros. They were not run.
- `RENDER_CLAMPED`: a server limit reduced the requested resolution.
  `detail` has `requested_dpi` and `effective_dpi`.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed, for example no `file` part or `options` is not valid JSON.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

ConversionTimeout.description:
The job did not finish within `timeout_seconds`. The engine process
was killed and replaced.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

example.error: the conversion did not finish within 120 seconds

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

InternalError.description: An unexpected failure inside the service. Details are logged under the request ID and not returned.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service is starting, draining for shutdown, or has no healthy worker.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

TooManyRequests.description: All workers are busy and the wait queue is full. Retry after the indicated delay.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

Unauthorized.description: The API key is missing or wrong.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

Unprocessable.description:
The request was understood but cannot be carried out for this input.
Retrying the same request will fail the same way.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | An option is out of range, unknown, or `pages` selects nothing. |
| `PASSWORD_REQUIRED` | The file is encrypted and no `password` was sent. |
| `INVALID_PASSWORD` | The `password` does not open the file. |
| `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | The job would exceed a server limit, for example more pages to render than `limits.max_render_pages`. |
| `CONVERSION_FAILED` | The engine could not convert the document. It is corrupt, or it crashed the engine twice. |

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

conversionFailed.summary: The engine could not convert the file

value.error: the document could not be converted
the document is encrypted and no password was provided

UnsupportedFormat.description:
The detected file type is not on the allow-list. The message names
what was detected. `/v1/capabilities` lists what is accepted.

X-Request-ID.description: The correlation ID of this request.

ApiKeyBearer.description: The service API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`.
